Not every sniffle needs a cancellation 🤧

Moderate illness, like a cold, runny nose, or mild fever, is usually not a reason to delay childhood immunisations. If you're unsure, give your vaccinator a call before cancelling. Staying on schedule helps keep children protected from preventable diseases 💙

media_refs.alt: A girl with a runny nose next to a woman looking at her phone. Overlay text: Runny nose? Sniffles? No need to cancel your childs immunisation appointment. A digital reminder shows 'Immunisation appointment for Lily today at 10am' with 'Accept' and 'Decline' buttons.

content: Talk to your usual health provider or visit bookmyvaccine.nz to book your winter immunisations now.

content: Nitrous oxide regulatory changes: www.health.govt.nz/regulation-legislation/psychoactive-substances/nitrous-oxide/nitrous-oxide-regulatory-changes

📢 Tighter controls on nitrous oxide are now in force. 
New rules aim to reduce harm from misuse while supporting legitimate uses. Import approvals will be required.

 Alcohol Drug Helpline:
- 0800 787 797
- Free text 8681

For more information, see below (link in the comments below).

media_refs.alt: Alert square graphic with a blue gradient background and a dark blue bell icon at the top. Bold heading reads ‘ALERT’. Below, text states: ‘Tighter controls on nitrous oxide are now in force, to reduce the risk of serious harm.’ At the bottom are the Te Kāwanatanga o Aotearoa New Zealand Government logo and the Ministry of Health Manatū Hauora logo.

content: News article: www.health.govt.nz/news/alcohol-levy-confirmed-to-support-harm-reduction-across-communities

The alcohol levy has been updated for 2026/27 to maintain funding for services that reduce alcohol-related harm across New Zealand. 

The levy will be set at $17.135 million, a modest increase to maintain its real value and support continuation of existing programmes.  

News article below.

media_refs.alt: Announcement square graphic with a light grey background and a dark blue bell icon at the top. Bold heading reads ‘ANNOUNCEMENT’. Below, smaller text states: ‘Alcohol levy confirmed to support harm reduction across communities.’ At the bottom are the Te Kāwanatanga o Aotearoa New Zealand Government logo and the Ministry of Health Manatū Hauora logo.

content: You can find out more on how to protect your baby when sleeping on Hapai Te Haoura's webpage here. sudinationalcoordination.co.nz/safe-sleep/
Today (5 June) is Safe Sleep Day which focuses on raising awareness and ensuring every sleep a baby has is a safe sleep.  It is a good reminder to make sure we put our babies to sleep safely.

At the bottom are the New Zealand Government Te Kāwanatanga o Aotearoa and Ministry of Health Manatū Hauora logos.
